title: Access Exception Governance Handbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This handbook defines the governance model, operational procedures, and evidence orchestration for temporary access exceptions across Redwood Inference. It bridges RBAC and authorization policies, audit logging requirements, data residency constraints, secure SDLC touchpoints, and incident-response triggers. The document is oriented toward security reviewers, platform owners, engineering managers, and compliance auditors.

Goals

- Provide a standardized lifecycle for access exceptions (request -> approve -> monitor -> renew/close).
- Ensure every exception produces a machine-readable evidence bundle suitable for audits.
- Minimize blast radius with compensating controls and automated telemetry.
- Align retention of evidence with data residency and legal hold rules.

Scope

This handbook applies to:
- Any privileged or cross-tenant access to production systems (console, service accounts, SSH, database, S3/GCS buckets).
- Exceptions to least-privilege RBAC policies (temporary role elevation, bypassing MFA, cross-region data access).
- Teams provisioning or approving access for external vendors and contractors.

Out-of-scope: routine self-service access covered by entitlement tooling and auto-granted developer sandbox roles.

Roles and Responsibilities

- Requester: engineer or operator initiating the exception. Responsible for justification and end-time.
- Approver: one or more role owners (security approver + service owner). Must be an authorized approver in the Access Governance roster.
- Exception Owner: the person responsible for monitoring the exception while active.
- Evidence Custodian (Security Ops): ensures evidence bundles are captured and stored per retention policy.
- Audit Consumer: internal/external auditor or compliance team who validates exception evidence.

Policy: When to Use an Exception

Use exceptions only when the required activity cannot be achieved by existing roles, temporary service accounts, or a documented maintenance window. Common valid reasons: emergency incident remediation, one-off data migrations, controlled vendor debugging sessions. Invalid reasons: permanent access for convenience, bypassing review for scheduled deployments.

Lifecycle and Procedures

1) Request

- Submit via the Access Exception Form (internal UI) or the Access API. The minimum fields required: requester, affected resource(s), justification, start_time, end_time, risk_level (low/medium/high), proposed compensating controls, SLA for closure.
- Attach a runbook or playbook if the exception supports incident remediation.

2) Review and Approval

- Automated triage: the Access Governance service evaluates the request against policy rules (resource sensitivity, data residency flag, requested privilege). If data residency=="EU" and requestor region!=EU, escalate to Data Residency Approver.
- Manual approval: Security approver + service owner must sign off within 4 business hours for "emergency-high" and 48 hours for others. Approvals are recorded in the Access Ticketing system with approver comments.

3) Enforcement and Controls

- Enforce time-bounds using short-lived credentials (STS tokens, ephemeral service account keys). No permanent IAM changes for exceptions.
- Apply compensating controls per risk level:
  - Low: third-party logging enabled, reviewer sampling every 72 hours.
  - Medium: session recording + realtime alerting on anomalous commands.
  - High: pair operator model (2-person auth), full packet capture (where lawful), and dedicated monitoring channel to Security Ops.

4) Monitoring and Evidence Capture

- Audit Logs: enable detailed audit logging for the affected resources for the full duration of the exception plus the post-close retention window.
- Telemetry Collection: Access Governance triggers the centralized evidence pipeline to capture:
  - IAM change events (who, what, when)
  - Session metadata (IP, device, start/end, duration)
  - Command-level logs where available (e.g., kubectl exec, SQL statements — sanitized if necessary)
  - Related incident or runbook references
- Evidence Bundle: at exception activation, an evidence bundle ID is created. All logs and metadata are tagged with this bundle ID for easy retrieval.

5) Renewal and Closure

- Exceptions auto-expire at end_time. Prior to expiry, the Exception Owner must either close the request or submit a renewal (justification + new end_time). Renewal requires expedited approval and must include new evidence demonstrating continued need.
- Closure checklist: activity summary, evidence pointer(s), retrospective assessment of risk controls, lessons-learned for future policy updates.

6) Post-Closure Audit

- Within 5 business days of closure, Security Ops assembles the finalized evidence bundle and validates it against the audit checklist. If gaps are found, a post-closure review ticket is opened and ownership assigned.

Evidence Orchestration: Implementation Details

- Evidence Format: JSON-LD manifests plus compressed artifacts (logs, recordings). Each bundle contains a manifest with top-level fields: bundle_id, request_id, requester, approvers, resources, time_window, evidence_items[]. (Note: the manifest is machine-parsable but not included inline in this handbook.)

- Tagging Strategy: all log producers must add metadata tags: "access_exception_id", "requester_id", "resource_class", "data_residency". This allows the centralized log processor to assemble bundles without manual searches.

- Retention Mapping Table (examples)

  Resource Type | Default Evidence Retention | Residency Notes
  --------------|---------------------------|-------------------
  API audit logs | 365 days | Extend to 7 years for regulated EU customers on legal hold
  Session recordings | 180 days | Only retained where lawful; otherwise store pointers + sanitized metadata
  SQL query logs | 90 days | Mask PII before retention if applicable
  IAM change events | 5 years | Critical for entitlement audits

- Storage and Encryption: evidence bundles are stored in the Compliance Evidence Store (encrypted at rest with KMS keys tied to tenant region). Cross-region replication is disabled by default for bundles labeled with strong residency constraints.

Integration Points

- RBAC & Auth: access exceptions must be represented as ephemeral elevations in the IAM registry. Identity providers (Okta, internal SSO) must emit SAML/OIDC session IDs into the evidence manifest.

- Audit Logging Pipelines: the centralized audit pipeline (audit-collector) must expose an API endpoint /v1/evidence/collect that accepts log pointers and bundle_id. Teams must instrument services to call this endpoint when an exception is active.

- Secure SDLC: any pull request that introduces code paths enabling elevated access must reference an open exception or provide approval evidence. The CI pipeline enforces a gating check: if a change modifies privileged-role binding or access-control code, the PR must include an "exception_evidence_id" or a config flag showing role hardening and unit/integration tests.

- Incident Response: if an incident (severity >= P1) triggers an emergency exception, the incident commander must annotate the incident ticket with exception_id, and the incident response runbook must include steps to snapshot evidence bundle mid-incident.

Operational SLAs and Thresholds

- Approval SLA: Emergency-high: 4 business hours; All others: 48 business hours.
- Evidence Assembly SLA: Final evidence bundle assembled within 5 business days of exception closure.
- Retrospective Review: Any high-risk exception must have a retrospective within 10 business days.

Automation Recipes (examples)

1) CLI — create exception (simplified)

curl -X POST https://access.redwood.internal/v1/exceptions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"requester":"aisha.patel","resources":["/k8s/cluster/prod-01"],"start_time":"2027-01-11T09:00:00Z","end_time":"2027-01-11T17:00:00Z","risk_level":"medium","compensating_controls":["session_recording","deny_service_external_ingress"]}'

Response: {"request_id":"REQ-20270111-1234","bundle_id":"BUNDLE-20270111-5678","approval_url":"https://access.redwood.internal/approve/REQ-20270111-1234"}

2) Evidence collection API (pseudo)

POST /v1/evidence/collect
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "bundle_id": "BUNDLE-20270111-5678",
  "log_pointer": "s3://compliance-logs/2027/01/11/k8s-events.json.gz",
  "tags": ["access_exception_id:REQ-20270111-1234"]
}

Checklist for Secure-SDLC Touchpoints

- PRs that change RBAC must include: exception_evidence_id OR a security-approval comment & test matrix.
- CI must run an "access-impact analyzer" for infra-as-code diffs and block merges if high-risk changes lack approvals.
- Post-merge, CI triggers ephemeral repro environments using the same short-lived creds as in production to validate that compensating controls function.

Incident Response Considerations

- If anomalous activity is detected on an active exception, Security Ops will:
  1) immediately suspend the exception (automated via IAM revoke call);
  2) Snapshot all evidence with a "security_suspension" flag;
  3) Notify Incident Commander and start a forensic runbook.

- Legal hold: If an investigation or external subpoena requires preservation, mark the bundle with a legal_hold tag, extend retention per legal instruction, and notify Evidence Custodian.

Audit and Reporting

- Quarterly audit: Security produces a report of all exceptions, broken down by team, risk level, business justification, and any anomalous post-approval activity.

- Dashboard metrics (minimum): average approval time, active exceptions by team, exceptions by resource class, exceptions renewed, exceptions escalated to incident.

Training and Onboarding

- Annually, teams that commonly request exceptions (SRE, Platform, Data Engineering) must complete a short course: "Access Exception Governance". Completion records are kept in the LMS and included in evidence manifests where relevant.

Change Control and Exceptions to this Handbook

- This handbook is owned by Security (owner_team). Material changes require review by: Security Policy Council, Legal, and two engineering service owners. Minor clarifications can be published as amendments with a 7-day review window.

Appendices

A. Example Evidence Manifest (fields - descriptive only)
- bundle_id
- request_id
- requester
- approvers
- resource_list
- start_time, end_time
- retention_policy_id
- tags
- artifacts: [log_url, recording_url, snapshot_url]
- closure_summary

B. Quick Reference Table: Approvers by Resource Class
- Production Kubernetes cluster: Service Owner + Security Oncall (primary)
- Production Database: DBA Owner + Security Engineering
- Cross-region data transfer (EU<->US): Data Residency Approver + Legal

C. Contact List
- Security Ops (Evidence Custodian): security-evidence@redwood.ai
- Access Governance service owner: marcus.chen@redwood.ai
- Incident Commander rota: incident-commander@redwood.ai

Related Documents

- RBAC certification policy (rbac-and-auth/*)
- Audit pipeline ingestion spec (audit-logging/*)
- Data residency decision matrix (data-residency-and-retention/*)

End of handbook
